description: Functional evaluation suite for mongodb-operations-expert hub verifying spoke routing, architecture guidance, and domain invariants.

evals.name: mongodb-operations-e-spoke1-architectural-routing
evals.prompt: Our production system is experiencing integration challenges with cloud native database disaggregation. We need an authoritative architectural breakdown and implementation procedure.
evals.expected_output: Routes to references/cloud-native-database-disaggregation.md, providing domain architecture, operational guidelines, and configuration specifications.

assertions.name: spoke reference routing
assertions.check: identifies references/cloud-native-database-disaggregation.md as the target reference file

assertions.name: architectural breakdown specification
assertions.check: provides structured guidance detailing core architecture components

assertions.name: domain configuration guidance
assertions.check: specifies concrete configuration directives or implementation parameters

assertions.name: no unverified assumptions
assertions.check: does not recommend unverified deprecated patterns or non-standard protocols

evals.name: mongodb-operations-e-spoke2-production-configuration
evals.prompt: We are deploying a high-reliability setup utilizing database migrations. What core patterns and failure recovery mechanisms must be configured?
evals.expected_output: Routes to references/database-migrations.md, detailing high-availability patterns, error handling, and recovery mechanisms.

assertions.name: spoke reference identification
assertions.check: identifies references/database-migrations.md as authoritative

assertions.name: failure recovery specification
assertions.check: explains failover, retry handling, or fault tolerance mechanics

assertions.name: production hardening directives
assertions.check: provides explicit reliability or security hardening recommendations

assertions.name: no manual error suppression
assertions.check: does not advise ignoring exceptions or silencing failure alerts

evals.name: mongodb-operations-e-spoke3-optimization-and-troubleshooting
evals.prompt: Our team is troubleshooting latency and throughput bottlenecks under heavy workload involving htap disaggregated storage. How do we isolate and resolve the root cause?
evals.expected_output: Routes to references/htap-disaggregated-storage.md, detailing diagnostic commands, profiling techniques, and performance optimization parameters.

assertions.name: troubleshooting spoke reference
assertions.check: identifies references/htap-disaggregated-storage.md as the target spoke

assertions.name: diagnostic procedure specification
assertions.check: specifies systematic inspection steps or diagnostic profiling tools

assertions.name: performance parameter tuning
assertions.check: identifies specific tuning parameters, caching layers, or concurrency limits

assertions.name: no blind resource overprovisioning
assertions.check: does not recommend blindly increasing memory or CPU without diagnostic evidence

evals.name: mongodb-operations-e-cost-invoice-tags-routing
evals.prompt: Finance wants our Atlas spend split by team. Which Atlas tooling gives us invoice line items per cluster, and how do resource tags show up in that data?
evals.expected_output: Routes to references/atlas-billing-mechanics-and-cost-visibility.md and explains Cost Explorer (UI and async Admin API), Tag/<key> invoice CSV columns, and the export-time tag snapshot.

assertions.name: billing spoke routing
assertions.check: identifies references/atlas-billing-mechanics-and-cost-visibility.md as the target reference file

assertions.name: tag columns
assertions.check: states that cluster tags appear as Tag/<key> columns in the invoice CSV and in results.lineItems.tags from the Admin API

assertions.name: export-time snapshot
assertions.check: warns that tags are read at export or API-call time, so retagging mid-cycle changes the whole invoice view

assertions.name: no spend cap claim
assertions.check: does not claim that Atlas billing alerts can stop, pause, or cap spend

evals.name: mongodb-operations-e-cost-commitment-drawdown-honesty
evals.prompt: We have an AWS EDP commitment and run Atlas on AWS. If we buy Atlas through the AWS Marketplace, will that draw down our EDP?
evals.expected_output: Routes to references/atlas-cost-commitments-cross-org-billing-and-finops-tooling.md and says AWS EDP drawdown for Atlas was not researched, so the answer must be confirmed with the MongoDB and AWS account teams.

assertions.name: commitments spoke routing
assertions.check: identifies references/atlas-cost-commitments-cross-org-billing-and-finops-tooling.md as the target reference file

assertions.name: AWS gap stated
assertions.check: states that AWS EDP drawdown for Atlas is not covered or verified by the reference and must be confirmed with the MongoDB and AWS account teams

assertions.name: comparison cases
assertions.check: contrasts the researched cases: Azure MACC eligibility is per offer, and Google Minimum Commitment drawdown caps channel private offers at 25% of the commitment

assertions.name: no invented answer
assertions.check: does not state as fact that Atlas spend retires an AWS EDP commitment

evals.name: mongodb-operations-e-cost-storage-levers-routing
evals.prompt: We keep three years of event data on a large Atlas cluster and want to cut the storage bill. How do deleting with TTL, Online Archive, and Data Federation compare on cost?
evals.expected_output: Routes to references/storage-and-data-lifecycle-cost-levers.md and compares the three cost models, including Data Federation at $5/TB processed and Online Archive per-GB storage with query limits.

assertions.name: storage levers routing
assertions.check: identifies references/storage-and-data-lifecycle-cost-levers.md as the target reference file

assertions.name: three-way cost model
assertions.check: compares TTL delete, Online Archive, and Data Federation on cost, naming the $5/TB processed Data Federation rate and per-GB archive storage

assertions.name: compression lever
assertions.check: mentions WiredTiger block compression (snappy, zlib, zstd) or index pruning with $indexStats as additional storage levers

assertions.name: hands off feature setup
assertions.check: points Online Archive rule configuration to mongodb-atlas-expert instead of explaining rule syntax
